## Listening to a metronome while you play

ReaScratch can play a click in the headphones on a deck's beats. The beats are the deck's own (its BPM and beat grid, or its beat map for a song whose tempo changes), and the first beat of each bar (the thicker line on the waveform) is higher. REAPER's own metronome only sounds while REAPER plays or records; the ReaScratch decks play with REAPER stopped, so you do not hear REAPER's metronome.

- **On/off**: the `N` key, a click on the window in the record's corner, or a MIDI button entered as `METRONOME button` in the `Metronome` group of the setup screen's `More` tab (its channel and note). Most controllers get one from their preset ("Metronome and preview buttons by controller"). With two controllers, the second APC40's `METRONOME` button switches it ([“Two controllers at once”](controller-setup-and-midi-mapping.md#two-controllers-at-once-eg-reloop-buddy--apc40-mkii)). While it is on, the rim of the window in the record's corner glows in the lamp colour, brighter for a moment each time a click sounds on this deck's beats.
- **The sample needs a BPM.** A sample without one gets no clicks (tap `T`, or enter it in setup).
- The settings are in the `Metronome` group of the setup screen's `More` tab. Deck A's settings work for both decks (changing them on deck B's screen changes deck A's).

| Setting | Choices | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `Metronome` | On/off | Off |
| `Metronome follows` | `Playing deck` = the beats of the deck that plays (both playing: the one that started first; both stopped: the one that played last) / `SYNC base deck` = the deck the other deck follows with SYNC (without SYNC, as `Playing deck`) / `Each deck` = each deck on its own (its own on/off, its own beats) | Playing deck |
| `Metronome out` | `Headphones` = the headphones only / `Headphones and main` = the headphones and the main output | Headphones |
| `Stopped / in hand` | `Keeps time` = it keeps clicking at the deck's BPM while the deck is stopped, touched or searched / `Silent` = no clicks then | Keeps time |
| `Metronome volume` | −30 to 0 dB | −12 dB |

- While the deck plays, the clicks fall exactly on the beats of the read position. Jumping onto a beat with a hot cue or a loop clicks too. With `Keeps time`, after you stop or touch the deck it keeps clicking at the deck's BPM; when it plays again, the clicks follow the beats of the read position again.
- In the headphones, the click sounds at the same volume wherever the `Cue mix` of the `Cue` track is set, and `Headphones and main` does not change its level there.
- Without headphones (no `Cue` track), set `Metronome out` to `Headphones and main` to hear it in the main output. A click in the main output is also in the "Rec Mix" track (the finished sound) of a performance capture, but not in the "Rec A" and "Rec B" tracks of the decks.
- In a project set up before 0.7, the video sync script adds the sends from each deck's channels 7/8 to the `Cue` track when it runs (no need to run setup again).

### Metronome and preview buttons by controller

Choosing a preset also sets the metronome on/off button and the preview button. For the metronome, a beat button (SYNC, TAP and so on) pressed with `SHIFT` came first; where none was free, an unused button. For the preview: on controllers with pad mode buttons and `LOAD`, `LOAD` pressed while holding the mode button; on the others, an unused button. Where it says none, or to use another button, enter it on the setup screen's `More` tab (the metronome in the `Metronome` group, the preview in the `Browser` group). In brackets: the channel and note as setup shows them. On controllers marked ⚠︎ (not tried on hardware) the numbers come from their documents. A button pressed with `SHIFT` may not light on some controllers.
